rows.title: Does Fort Collins have a ban on electronic billboards?
rows.standfirst: Yes. Fort Collins prohibits billboards with displays that are more than 50% electronic, though government land is exempt from the ban.

rows.title: New political players have upended a fragile peace in Colorado’s oil and gas wars
rows.standfirst: Operators and environmentalists have over 20 years maneuvered into a delicate balance. Now they’re aligned in opposition to a third-party ballot measure guaranteeing Coloradans’ right to natural gas.

rows.title: Jared Polis signs bill giving Colorado artists creative control with new business structure
rows.standfirst: Colorado is the first state to create “A Corps” or artist companies, a subset of limited liability corporations that keep creative control of companies in the hands of the artists

rows.title: Xcel Energy customers may be hit with the largest electric rate increase ever
rows.standfirst: The $225 million increase would raise the average residential bill by $6.13, but the proposed rate needs PUC approval and consumer advocates oppose it

rows.title: Visits to Colorado ski resorts collapsed in 2025-26 with the steepest annual decline in decades
rows.standfirst: It was the lowest showing for Colorado ski areas since 1991-92

rows.title: Watch: AI leaders discuss technology in every day life at Colorado SunFest 2026
rows.standfirst: Dr. Mohammad Mahor and Jon Nordmark discussed how Artificial Intelligence is used in every day life at Colorado SunFest 2026.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado teens take different path to summer jobs — networking, entrepreneurship and asking a CEO
rows.standfirst: It’s rough out in the job market, especially for teenage workers as summer jobs drop to a 78-year low. Plus: Denver ranks 2nd for employers who expect to rehire after AI job cuts.

rows.title: Are less-thirsty crops a solution to Colorado’s growing water problems?
rows.standfirst: The state’s resilient, adaptable farmers can raise just about anything and use less water doing it. But will enough people buy what they produce?

rows.title: Denver-area inflation increases to 5%. Blame energy costs.
rows.standfirst: Biggest contributors to higher prices are the cost of gas and energy, which increased at double-digit rates. Food costs were also higher, growing 1.8% in the past year.

rows.title: What’s Working: Uneven inflation still eroding affordability in Colorado
rows.standfirst: Reports on the state’s affordability issues keep coming. Plus: Weld and Douglas counties see employment growth, but other large counties? Not so much.

rows.title: What the heck is happening in downtown Denver?
rows.standfirst: Neither empty nor bustling, the city continues its urban recovery in order, as one official tells it, to “control our own destiny.” Here’s the story so far.

rows.title: Roan Plateau parcels proposed for oil and gas lease sales, undoing protections for iconic western Colorado mesa
rows.standfirst: The planned sale covering 127,000 acres, including 5,000 acres on the plateau, is the result of federal legislation requiring quarterly lease sales in nine Western states, including Colorado

rows.title: Who’s ready to picnic in downtown Denver’s Civic Center park?
rows.standfirst: A massive transformation of the downtown Denver park known in recent history for drug deals and crime is underway, but can the city change longtime perceptions?

rows.title: Owner of Denver Post agrees to $13.5 million settlement with city over unpaid rent, will remove sign
rows.standfirst: The newspaper’s lease was supposed to go through 2029, but it will now end June 30

rows.title: A new era for downtown Denver’s biggest mall is beginning to take shape
rows.standfirst: Denver Pavilions, downtown’s signature outdoor mall, is finding a new identity amid a turbulent time for the center of the city

rows.title: Rural is Rad initiative champions small-town outdoor brands with a big debut at Outside Days festival
rows.standfirst: A new collective hopes to build a pathway to keeping Colorado’s small-town creators in the places that inspired their inventions

rows.title: New homes and businesses in Denver will see major surge in water connection fees
rows.standfirst: The increases take effect July 1, and come as Colorado cities wrestle with the expense of new reservoirs and high housing costs

rows.title: What’s Working: Why hamburgers cost more today
rows.standfirst: Consumers yearn for steaks at lower prices. But demand is outpacing a shrinking supply. Plus: $250 bonus for young Denver workers, quantum-tech grants and thwarting rent-setting schemes

rows.title: Colorado helium reserves got big boost when war with Iran cut off 30% of the world’s supply
rows.standfirst: Southeastern Colorado has been producing helium for two decades, but when the Strait of Hormuz was closed, it suddenly became a lot more valuable

rows.title: Sportsbooks have spent about $1.5M on Democratic, Republican statehouse primaries in Colorado
rows.standfirst: The state-level super PAC American Future is funded by a federal super PAC of the same name that has received millions of dollars from the sports betting companies DraftKings, FanDuel and Fanatics

rows.title: Eastern Colorado farmers brace for worst wheat harvest since 1965
rows.standfirst: In the heart of Colorado wheat country, only about half the typical precipitation has fallen this year, forcing farmers to make hard choices

rows.title: Universal basic food pilot program tackles food insecurity in new way
rows.standfirst: A year-long pilot provided no-cost groceries to people in Denver and Del Norte, aiming to help people struggling to make ends meet — even if they aren’t eligible for SNAP

rows.title: Regulators cut Colorado oil and gas firms’ fines to $2M after settlements
rows.standfirst: Six oil and gas operators were facing $11 million in fines for falsified reports involving soil, groundwater and organic contaminant sampling tests

rows.title: Can a giant robot glue gun help solve Colorado’s housing crisis?
rows.standfirst: Azure’s 3D printers in Montbello can build a $70,000 home out of 100,000 recycled plastic bottles in just a couple of days.

rows.title: Takeover reports send Vail Resorts stock up as CEO Rob Katz defends network of 42 ski areas as “the heart of our business model”
rows.standfirst: The largest resort operator in North America saw its best day on Wall Street in several years as calls increase for the company to start selling resorts

rows.title: Did long-term unemployment rise in the US in the past year?
rows.standfirst: Yes. The number of people in long-term unemployment has increased significantly compared with a year ago.

rows.title: What’s Working: In Fraser, the arts — and a sprawling new arts center — become the town’s identity
rows.standfirst: Although the town’s fame as “Icebox of the Nation” is catchy too. Plus: Colorado’s July Fourth cookout costs less than last year, more downtown Denver investments, Colorado’s 1-year job growth at 0%, and more!

rows.title: Could a new Denver data center use up to 800,000 gallons of water a day?
rows.standfirst: Yes. A new data center in north Denver could use up to 805,000 gallons of water each day if all three planned buildings are constructed.

rows.title: Here’s what it costs to run a daycare in Colorado’s most expensive county
rows.standfirst: Childcare costs in Boulder County are almost double the state average. Providers are looking for new revenue sources as government help for families dwindles.

rows.title: Aspen Snowmass hopes to battle warmer winters by storing snow. Here’s how.
rows.standfirst: If the new storage system works, terrain parks at Buttermilk and Snowmass will be built next season using last season’s snow
